What changed with continuous state and depth?

New numerical report and six curves · New frame explorer · Comparison numbers (JSON)

What is comparable

The previous combined norm covers RGB + eight discrete state-value embeddings. The new combined norm covers RGB + one projected continuous-state embedding + real depth features. Those combined norms use different representations; a change in magnitude alone does not establish a behavior change. RGB-only gradients share the same input coordinates. Neither measure is a gradient in physical joint, pixel or depth units.

Same frame identities, text, metadata, recorded progress and terminals are checked explicitly. Both checkpoints are at step 2000. Training randomness and architecture changes are bundled here; this is not a controlled attribution to depth alone. These 128 training + 8 validation episodes are a ReBot survey, not the 40/20/40 training mixture.

Progress profiles on identical frames

— Previous critic— New critic

Raw gradient norms on a log axis; no rescaling or smoothing. Equal-width progress bins, frame medians, empty bins break the line. Hover for exact medians and counts. Click a new-critic point to inspect the bin's frames. Episode-balanced curves and IQR are in the full numerical report.

Rank associations by action

All entries are Spearman correlations except overlap. Old → new uses each checkpoint's combined norm, value and advantage. Absolute advantage excludes terminal transitions. Paired rank compares which same frames have large gradients; top-10% overlap reports shared membership, with stable tie-breaking. Click an action to inspect its curve. Counts are descriptive, not independent trials.

Depth: small local gradient, measurable finite effect

The check uses the 10%, 50% and 90% temporal anchors in each validation episode, chosen without looking at gradients. Three of the 24 frames already lack depth; substitution and saturation summaries use the remaining 21 real-depth frames. Only depth presence is changed; the model substitutes its learned missing-depth bank. This is an input intervention, not a measure of prediction quality. Values are computed at the checkpoint's inference precision, so tiny differences can round to zero.
